question.worked_solution:
The stationary points of a multivariable function $f$ are the points $a$ in the domain of $f$ such that ${f}^{′}(a)={0}^{T},$ where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}.
$$

In this case, the domain of $f$ is $D=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}∣y>0\},$ and the first partial derivatives of $f$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2x+y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =x+\frac{2}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the first derivative of $f$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x+y & x+\frac{2}{y}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the stationary points, we need to find the points where ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T}.$
Setting ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T},$ we have the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y=0 \\ x+\frac{2}{y}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $y$ in the first equation, we get

$$
2x+y=0\,⟹\,y=-2x.
$$

Then, substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{2}{-2x} & =0 \\ x-\frac{1}{x} & =0 \\ x & =\frac{1}{x} \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Back-substituting these values into $y=-2x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=-1 & \,⟹\,y=-2(-1)=2 \\ x=1 & \,⟹\,y=-2(1)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our system has two solutions, $(-1,2)$ and $(1,-2).$ We reject the point $(1,-2)$ because it does not lie in the domain of $f(x,y).$

In conclusion, $f$ has one stationary point, $(-1,2).$
